headline: High-risk pair: ECC can write shared files and use MCP while PaddleOCR processes documents, creating default-path prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers; PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If ECC feeds OCR outputs into prompts or MCP workflows, document content can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF ECC ingests PaddleOCR output from a shared file or MCP channel without provenance tagging, prompt injection is possible.
IF PaddleOCR output contains attacker-controlled text and ECC treats it as instructions, the pathway activates.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before ECC consumes OCR text.
Prefix OCR outputs with a non-executable delimiter and provenance label.
Store OCR outputs in a separate folder from prompt inputs.
Disable MCP handoff for untrusted documents.
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks between OCR and agent prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, git history, code, documentation, and security findings, and can write/read the filesystem. PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If they share a workspace, sensitive document contents can flow into ECC logs or outputs. No isolation or redaction mechanism is documented, so leakage is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, document contents can be exposed to ECC.
IF ECC persists session summaries or metrics containing OCR text, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for OCR inputs and agent logs.
Redact sensitive fields before passing OCR text to ECC.
Review ECC session summaries after each run.
Restrict OCR jobs to non-sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: implement automatic data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can modify git state, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses; PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs. If both are pointed at the same repo or output directory, they can overwrite artifacts or race on shared files. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is a realistic default-path risk.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file overwrites or races can occur.
IF ECC commits while PaddleOCR-generated artifacts are still being written, git state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize runs so only one agent writes at a time.
Pause git commits until OCR artifacts are finalized.
Use temporary files then atomic renames.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and act on session summaries, skills, and security findings, while PaddleOCR converts documents/images into text. If ECC treats OCR output as authoritative, OCR mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or commits. Because ECC has write and git capabilities, the blast radius can be irreversible without explicit verification.
conditions: IF ECC uses PaddleOCR text as source-of-truth without verification, downstream errors propagate.
IF ECC commits or edits based on OCR output, incorrect text can become persistent.
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on OCR text.
Compare OCR output against the source document for critical fields.
Limit ECC to drafting, not committing, from OCR results.
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for review.
requires-engineering: add confidence-aware gating before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session summaries, security findings, and git history, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. A compliance issue arises only if regulated documents are routed through ECC logs or retained in session artifacts. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so this is a limited overlap rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed and ECC stores them in session summaries or git history, retention/compliance issues arise.
IF document images contain personal data and are retained beyond policy, compliance exposure occurs.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated documents through ECC.
Delete session artifacts after each OCR task.
Keep OCR outputs out of git history.
Review retention settings before processing sensitive files.
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention controls.
